beats.text: It's Monday, nineteen hundred. Anna is doing the laundry, and it will take her the whole day.
One load needs fifty gallons of water, carried in by hand.
Water was hauled, heated on the stove, scrubbed, boiled and wrung.
But that was just one load. In a year, a housewife carried thirty-six tons of water.
So Monday was wash day, every single week.
Then came running water, electricity, and the washing machine.
Today, you press one button, and you don't even have to watch.
Anna's whole day is your one button.

sources: One load of laundry (washing, boiling, rinsing) used about 50 gallons of water; over a year a housewife walked 148 miles toting water and carried over 36 tons of water. Digital History, University of Houston, 'Private Life' (based on Susan Strasser, Never Done: A History of American Housework, 1982).
Anna is illustrative. 'Monday was wash day': common household routine around 1900 (Strasser 1982). Total housework hours 1900 vs. today are disputed (Lebergott vs. Ramey 2009) – not used.
